question: What makes the intramuscular route absorb medications faster than the subcutaneous route?

options.A: Muscles have a richer blood supply than fat tissue
options.C: Muscle tissue contains more nerve endings
options.D: Injections go straight into the main arteries

explanation: Skeletal muscle has a dense network of blood vessels that quickly take up and distribute injected medications compared to fatty layers. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h1)

question: Why does the choice of the muscle site affect how fast a drug works?

options.A: Thicker muscles destroy the active drug ingredients
options.B: Some muscle fibers actively push the medicine out
options.C: Certain sites completely block liquid absorption
options.D: Different muscles have different levels of blood supply

explanation: Blood flow drives absorption speed, so a site with poor circulation will slow down how fast the drug enters the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h1)

question: Which injection site is generally considered the safest for adult patients?
explanation: The ventrogluteal site lacks major nerves and large blood vessels, making it the preferred and safest choice for adults. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h2)

question: A nurse needs to give an IM vaccine to a healthy adult. Which site is the most appropriate choice?
explanation: The deltoid muscle is easily accessible and standard for routine adult vaccinations like tetanus or influenza. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h2)

question: If a needle has a lower gauge number, what does that tell you about its size?
explanation: Needle gauges can be tricky! Just remember: the smaller the gauge number (like 20G), the thicker and wider the needle is. A higher number (like 25G) is much thinner.

question: What is the main risk of using a needle that is too short for an intramuscular injection?

options.A: The medicine will absorb too fast into the bloodstream
options.B: Medication enters the subcutaneous fat instead of muscle
options.C: The needle will bend or break inside the bone
options.D: Blood will flow backwards into the syringe instantly

explanation: If the needle fails to pierce past the subcutaneous tissue, the drug deposits in the fat, causing irritation and altered absorption. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h3)

question: At what angle should an intramuscular injection be inserted into the skin?
explanation: A perpendicular 90-degree angle ensures the needle penetrates deep enough to reach the muscle layer beneath the skin and fat. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of using the Z-track technique during an IM injection?

options.A: To push the needle deeper into the major blood vessels
options.B: To stretch the skin so the needle insertion causes no pain
options.C: To make it easier to aspirate blood before injecting
options.D: To seal the medication inside the muscle and prevent skin staining

explanation: Pulling the skin sideways before insertion offsets the tissue layers, sealing the track so irritating drugs cannot leak upward. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is a major cause of accidental needlestick injuries during injections?
explanation: Attempting to put the cap back onto a used needle frequently leads to accidental punctures to the fingers and hands. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h5)

question: Why must the antiseptic skin prep dry completely before the needle enters?

options.A: To prevent the alcohol from destroying the medication
options.B: To cool down the muscle tissue for less pain
options.C: To make the skin slippery so the needle enters smoother
options.D: To allow the antiseptic time to kill microbes and prevent stinging

explanation: Chemical disinfectants need contact time to eliminate surface pathogens, and wet alcohol entering a puncture wound causes sharp pain. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h5)

question: A patient cries out with sharp, shooting pain down their leg while receiving an IM injection in the buttocks. What has most likely happened?

options.A: The needle has irritated or hit the sciatic nerve
options.B: The muscle is experiencing a normal cramp
options.C: The needle gauge is too small for the fluid
options.D: The medication is reacting with subcutaneous fat

explanation: Shooting pain down the leg is a classic sign of nerve trauma, specifically involving the sciatic nerve during poor dorsogluteal injections. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h6)

question: Which of these is a bad practice that can cause tissue damage when giving injections?

options.A: Rotating sites when patients need repeated doses
options.B: Using the correct needle length for the patient's size
options.C: Giving multiple injections into the exact same spot
options.D: Allowing the skin disinfectant to dry before piercing

explanation: Spot on! Poking the exact same spot over and over causes hard, damaged tissue and scars. Always rotate your injection sites to give the skin and muscle a break!
